svg.aria-label: Fig. M4 Inside a scheduler queue, wakeup, select and replay
svg.text: Fig. M4 Inside a scheduler queue, wakeup, select and replay
A matrix scheduler fits what is measured (operands read at issue, queues that do not shift). The entry format and the replay rule are proposed.
One queue entry (integer queue of about 13)
proposed on top of the patent reading
uop and immediate
dest preg
src A preg
rA
src B preg
rB
flags preg
shadow
v

rA, rB: ready bits set by wakeup. shadow: 3 bit timer counting down from a load this uop was woken by; while non zero the entry stays allocated after issue so it can reissue (proposed, from the patent).
Operands are read from the register file at issue, not kept in the queue (Handley, measured), which keeps entries small and lets the file be banked.
Dependency matrix and age matrix, 13 x 13
patent reading, likely (KB)
dependency: row waits on column
entry 1 completes: column 1 clears, row 3 becomes ready
wakeup is a column clear, one wire per entry, no tag compare
age: row is older than column
select: the ready entry with no older ready entry
allocation writes one row and one column; no shifting
Two level reservation station (patent): a small primary buffer holds the highest priority ops, a secondary the rest; secondary picks fill
slots the primary leaves empty. Whether the 13 is the primary or the sum is open; I draw it as the sum.
Pairing, the size dispute and the load shadow
Paired queues (inferred)
Q1 with Q2, Q3 with Q4, Q5 with Q6
a queue with nothing ready issues from its partner
a shared age matrix across the pair would do it (mine)
The 13 vs 24/28 dispute
Johnson: 24 per int queue, 28 per mul queue
Handley: Johnson counts each pair twice, so 13
total 134 measured by Chen fits 6 x 13 + extra
I draw 13, and keep 134 as the hard number
Speculative wakeup behind a load (proposed from the patent)
load issues
AGU, L1D read
data, cycle 3
dep issues
ALU use
late tag check and store address recheck
replay
shadow window, dependents keep entries
The consumer is woken for cycle 3 on the assumption the load hits and its address check passes. A store
address resolving two to four cycles late causes a replay, not a flush (measured), which is the shadow at work.
The replaying load waits in a load execution queue bank of its pipe (patent).
Test for the shadow depth: a dependent chain of k ALU ops behind a load that replays once. Cost grows
with k until k exceeds the shadow depth, then the extra ops were never issued and cost nothing more.
One possibly mispredicting op issues per cycle; age bits built from short per entry offsets say which younger work to flush (patent).
Issue ports to the register file
Reads and writes per cycle (derived from the port map)
6 int + 4 fp + 4 ls units with up to 2 sources: 28 reads; 14 writes plus load data
4 banks in the integer file (patent) means about 7 reads per bank per cycle, too many for one bank
proposed: banks are split by physical register number mod 4 and a bank conflict stalls select by a cycle
test: a stream of ALU ops whose sources all map to one bank (hard to control) vs spread
Cross domain paths (measured)
int to SIMD goes through a load slot as a fake load, about 6 cycles
SIMD to int uses a dedicated path, about 6 cycles
a MADD feeds the next addend in 1 cycle, so the multiplier has an accumulate bypass
int divide is a side pipe behind unit 5, one divide every 2 cycles, unit 5 keeps taking other work
● confirmed, 3+ measurements
◆ corroborated, 2 sources
